lessons.name: What is DevOps — Culture, Principles, CALMS Framework
lessons.desc: DevOps is a cultural and technical movement that breaks down silos between development and operations. CALMS: Culture, Automation, Lean, Measurement, Sharing.
lessons.q: Explain the CALMS framework and how it applies to DevOps adoption.
lessons.qsub: How does DevOps eliminate the "throw over the wall" mentality? What does "you build it, you run it" mean in practice?
terms: You build it, you run it
Dev team production ki ownership leti hai.
Dev aur Ops ke beech deewar.
lessons.what:
Definition: DevOps ek culture + practices ka set hai jo development aur operations ko jodta hai taaki software tez, safe aur baar-baar deliver ho. CALMS framework adoption ko check karne ka tareeka hai.

Purane model mein dev code 'deewar ke upar se phenk' deta tha aur ops ko sambhalna padta tha.
lessons.why: Chhote, frequent releases risk kam karte hain aur feedback jaldi milta hai.
lessons.code:
# DevOps loop
plan -> code -> build -> test -> release -> deploy -> operate -> monitor -> (feedback) -> plan

# Example: har merge par
git push -> CI (build+test) -> CD (staging) -> canary -> prod -> alerts
gotchas: DevOps ek job title/tool nahi, culture hai
Automation bina measurement ke andhi hai
'DevOps team' banana naya silo ban sakta hai

lessons.name: DevOps vs SRE vs Platform Engineering
lessons.desc: DevOps is the philosophy. SRE applies software engineering to operations. Platform Engineering builds internal developer platforms (IDPs) for self-service.
lessons.q: What is the difference between DevOps, SRE, and Platform Engineering?
lessons.qsub: How do you decide which operating model to adopt based on organizational maturity?
terms: Ops ko software engineering se; SLOs, error budgets.
lessons.what: Definition: DevOps 'kya aur kyun', SRE 'reliability ko measurable bana kar kaise' (SLI/SLO/error budget), Platform Engineering 'developers ke liye golden paths/portal' hai.
lessons.why: Interview mein teeno ka fark aur overlap clear batana zaroori hai.
lessons.code:
SLO: 99.9% requests < 300ms (30 days)
Error budget = 0.1% = ~43 min/month
Budget khatam -> feature releases roko, reliability work

Platform: `make service name=orders` -> repo + CI + k8s + dashboards ready
gotchas: SRE ≠ ops team ka naya naam
Error budget policy tabhi kaam karti jab management maane
Platform ko product ki tarah treat karo

lessons.name: SDLC Automation & Delivery Pipeline
lessons.desc: The software delivery lifecycle: plan → code → build → test → release → deploy → operate → monitor. Automation at every stage reduces lead time and errors.
lessons.q: Walk through the SDLC pipeline from commit to production. What metrics define elite performance?
lessons.qsub: What is shift-left and how does it affect pipeline design?
lessons.what: Definition: Plan → code → build → test → release → deploy → operate. Har stage automate; fast tests pehle, slow tests baad mein.
lessons.why: Manual steps error aur delay laate hain.
lessons.code:
stages: [lint, unit, build, integration, security, deploy-staging, e2e, deploy-prod]
# fast checks pehle: lint/unit < 5 min
gotchas: Flaky tests pipeline ka trust todte hain
Pipeline 10 min se upar ho to developers bypass karte hain

lessons.name: Trunk-based Development & Feature Flags
lessons.desc: Trunk-based development: short-lived branches merged to main frequently. Feature flags decouple deployment from release — merge dark code, turn on later.
lessons.q: What is trunk-based development and how do feature flags enable it?
lessons.qsub: How do you manage flag debt and prevent stale feature flags from accumulating?
terms: Short-lived branches, main par frequent merge.
lessons.what: Definition: Developers din mein kai baar main mein merge karte hain; incomplete features flags ke peeche. Release = flag on, deploy = code shipping — dono alag.
lessons.why: Integration problems jaldi pakadte hain; CI/CD ke liye zaroori.

lessons.name: DORA Metrics — Measuring DevOps Performance
lessons.desc: DORA identifies four key metrics: Deployment Frequency, Lead Time for Changes, Change Failure Rate, Time to Restore Service.
lessons.q: What are the four DORA metrics and what benchmarks define elite performance?
lessons.qsub: How do DORA metrics relate to the SPACE framework for developer productivity?
terms: Kitne deploys fail; recover kitne time mein.
lessons.what: Definition: DORA ke 4 metrics: deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate, time to restore. Elite teams speed aur stability dono mein achhi hoti hain.
lessons.why: Objectively dekhne ke liye ki delivery improve ho rahi hai ya nahi.
lessons.code:
deploys/week = count(prod_deploys)
lead_time   = median(deploy_ts - first_commit_ts)
CFR         = failed_deploys / deploys
MTTR        = median(restore_ts - incident_ts)
cons: Individuals ko judge karne ke liye galat
gotchas: Goodhart's law: target banate hi gaming
Speed aur stability trade-off nahi, saath badhte hain

lessons.name: CI/CD Pipeline Design — Stages, Gates, Artifact Promotion
lessons.desc: CI (Continuous Integration): merge frequently, build and test every change. CD (Continuous Delivery): every change is deployable but release is manual.
lessons.q: Design a CI/CD pipeline from scratch. What are the key stages and gates?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between Continuous Delivery and Continuous Deployment?
lessons.what: Definition: Build once, promote same artifact across environments (dev→staging→prod). Gates: tests, scans, approvals. Artifact immutable.
lessons.why: 'Staging mein chala, prod mein nahi' tab hota hai jab har env ke liye alag build ho.
lessons.code:
build -> image:sha-abc123 (ek baar)
deploy staging (image:sha-abc123 + staging config)
deploy prod    (image:sha-abc123 + prod config)

lessons.name: GitHub Actions — Workflows, Runners, Matrix Builds
lessons.desc: GitHub Actions is CI/CD natively integrated with GitHub. Workflows are YAML with triggers, jobs, steps. Runners can be GitHub-hosted or self-hosted.
lessons.q: How do you design an efficient GitHub Actions workflow? Explain matrix builds and caching.
lessons.qsub: When would you use self-hosted runners over GitHub-hosted runners?
lessons.what: Definition: Events (push, PR) par jobs/steps chalte hain. Matrix builds, caching, secrets, reusable workflows, environments with approvals.
lessons.why: GitHub ke saath tight integration, setup kam.
lessons.code:
name: ci
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy: { matrix: { node: [18, 20] } }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}, cache: npm }
      - run: npm ci && npm test
gotchas: Secrets forks ko expose nahi hote

lessons.name: Deployment Strategies — Blue/Green, Canary, Rolling, A/B
lessons.desc: Blue/green: two identical environments, switch traffic. Canary: percentage of traffic to new version. Rolling: gradually replace instances.
lessons.q: Compare blue/green, canary, and rolling deployment strategies. When would you choose each?
lessons.qsub: How does Kubernetes implement rolling updates with maxSurge and maxUnavailable?
lessons.what: Definition: Blue/green instant rollback deta hai par double capacity. Canary real traffic par risk kam karta hai. Rolling default K8s strategy. A/B experiments ke liye.
lessons.why: Release risk aur downtime kam karne ke liye.
lessons.code:
# Argo Rollouts canary
steps:
  - setWeight: 5
  - pause: { duration: 10m }
  - setWeight: 25
  - analysis: success-rate > 99%
  - setWeight: 100

lessons.name: Artifact Management — Versioning, Registries, Immutability
lessons.desc: Artifacts are versioned, signed, and stored in registries. Immutability: once tagged/pushed, artifact never changes.
lessons.q: Why is artifact immutability critical for reproducible deployments? How do you enforce it?
lessons.qsub: What is SBOM and how does it relate to software supply chain security?
lessons.what: Definition: Har build ek versioned artifact (image digest/SHA). Immutable tags, signed, retention policy, vulnerability scan registry mein.
lessons.why: Jo test hua wahi prod mein jaye — traceability.
lessons.code:
docker build -t registry/app:1.4.2-abc123 .
docker push registry/app:1.4.2-abc123
cosign sign registry/app@sha256:...
# k8s: image digest se pin
gotchas: Retention policy nahi to storage cost

lessons.name: Pipeline Security — SAST, DAST, SBOM, Supply Chain
lessons.desc: SAST scans source code. DAST scans running app. SBOM catalogs dependencies. Supply chain security ensures trusted artifacts.
lessons.q: How do you build security into a CI/CD pipeline? Explain SAST, DAST, and SCA.
lessons.qsub: What is the SLSA framework and how does it improve supply chain security?
lessons.what: Definition: Pipeline mein secrets scan, SAST, SCA, container scan, DAST, signing aur provenance (SLSA). Pipeline khud bhi attack target hai — least privilege tokens.
lessons.why: Supply chain attacks build system se aate hain.
lessons.code:
- gitleaks
- semgrep
- trivy image app:sha
- syft -> sbom
- cosign sign
# OIDC se short-lived cloud creds (long-lived keys nahi)
gotchas: Gate failure ko ignore karne ka tareeka na ho
PR from forks ko secrets nahi

lessons.name: Docker Architecture — Images, Layers, Union FS, Overlay2
lessons.desc: Docker images are read-only layers built from a Dockerfile. Each instruction creates a layer. Union filesystem (overlay2) merges layers.
lessons.q: Explain Docker image layers and how the overlay2 filesystem works.
lessons.qsub: What is copy-on-write and how does it affect container performance?
terms: Union filesystem — layers stack + writable top layer.
lessons.what: Definition: Image layers ka stack hai, container = image + writable layer. Layers cache aur share hote hain. Containers namespaces (isolation) aur cgroups (resource limits) use karte hain.
lessons.why: Layer samajhna build speed aur image size optimize karne ki jad hai.
lessons.code:
$ docker history app:1.0          # layers dekho
$ docker run -m 256m --cpus=0.5 app   # cgroup limits
$ docker inspect app | jq '.[0].GraphDriver'
cons: Shared kernel — VM jitna isolated nahi
gotchas: Delete karne se bhi pichli layer ka data image mein rehta hai
Writable layer ephemeral — volumes use karo

lessons.name: Dockerfile Best Practices — Multi-stage, Cache, Minimal Images
lessons.desc: Multi-stage builds: use one image to build and a separate minimal image to run. Result: tiny production images without build tools.
lessons.q: How do you write an optimized Dockerfile? Explain multi-stage builds and layer caching.
lessons.qsub: What is a distroless image and when would you use it vs a scratch image?
terms: Build stage alag, runtime stage chhota.
lessons.what: Definition: Dependencies pehle copy+install, phir source — cache hit zyada. Multi-stage se compilers final image mein nahi. .dockerignore, non-root user, pinned versions.
lessons.why: Chhoti image = fast pull, kam attack surface.
lessons.code:
FROM node:20 AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM node:20-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app/dist ./dist
COPY --from=build /app/node_modules ./node_modules
USER node
CMD ["node","dist/main.js"]
gotchas: COPY . . pehle likhne se cache toot-ta hai
Secrets build args mein mat daalo

lessons.name: Container Networking — Bridge, Host, Overlay, CNI
lessons.desc: Bridge: default network. Host: shares host network stack. Overlay: multi-host networking via VXLAN. CNI: standard interface for container networking.
lessons.q: Compare bridge, host, and overlay networking in Docker. When would you use each?
lessons.qsub: How does Docker DNS resolve container names and how does CNI differ from Docker networking?
terms: Container host network share karta hai.
lessons.what: Definition: Bridge network par containers apas mein naam se baat karte hain (user-defined bridge). Ports publish karke bahar. K8s mein CNI plugins pod networking dete hain.
lessons.why: Connectivity issues debug karna aur isolation design.
lessons.code:
$ docker network create appnet
$ docker run -d --network appnet --name db postgres
$ docker run -d --network appnet -p 8080:8080 api   # api -> db:5432
$ docker run --network host nginx   # port mapping nahi
gotchas: localhost container ke andar apna hi hota hai
Default bridge par DNS naam nahi
-p publish ke bina bahar se access nahi

lessons.name: Container Security — Non-root, Read-only FS, Seccomp, AppArmor
lessons.desc: Run containers as non-root user. Mount filesystem read-only where possible. Seccomp restricts syscalls. AppArmor/SELinux Mandatory Access Control.
lessons.q: List the key container security hardening techniques and why each matters.
lessons.qsub: What is a container breakout attack and how do capabilities like --cap-drop ALL prevent it?
lessons.what: Definition: Root user, privileged mode, docker.sock mount avoid. Read-only rootfs, capabilities drop, seccomp default profile, resource limits.
lessons.why: Container escape se host compromise ho sakta hai.
lessons.code:
docker run --read-only --cap-drop=ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges \
  --user 10001 --pids-limit 200 -m 256m app

lessons.name: Docker Compose & Local Development
lessons.desc: Docker Compose defines multi-container applications in YAML. Services, networks, volumes, environment variables configured in docker-compose.yml.
lessons.q: How do you set up a reproducible local development environment with Docker Compose?
lessons.qsub: What is Docker Compose watch and how does it improve the dev loop?
lessons.what: Definition: docker-compose.yml mein app + DB + cache ek command se. Local dev aur integration tests ke liye perfect; production orchestration nahi.
lessons.why: 'Mere machine par chalta hai' hatane ka sabse aasaan tareeka.
gotchas: depends_on ready hone ka wait nahi karta — healthcheck
Volume delete karoge to data jaayega

lessons.name: K8s Architecture — Control Plane, Nodes, etcd, Scheduler
lessons.desc: Control plane: API server, etcd, scheduler, controller manager. Workers: kubelet, kube-proxy, container runtime (containerd).
lessons.q: Explain the Kubernetes control plane components and their responsibilities.
lessons.qsub: How does etcd maintain consistency in a distributed K8s cluster?
lessons.what: Definition: Control plane: API server, etcd, scheduler, controller manager. Nodes: kubelet, container runtime, kube-proxy. Declarative model: desired state likho, controllers actual ko match karte hain.
lessons.why: Failures (pod pending, node not ready) debug karne ke liye architecture samajhna zaroori.
lessons.code:
$ kubectl get nodes
$ kubectl describe pod web-1      # events: scheduling, pull, probe
$ kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp

lessons.name: Pods, Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, Secrets
lessons.desc: Pod: smallest deployable unit. Deployment: declarative updates for Pods. Service: stable network endpoint for a set of Pods.
lessons.q: Explain the relationship between Pods, Deployments, and Services in Kubernetes.
lessons.qsub: How do liveness, readiness, and startup probes differ and when do you use each?
lessons.what: Definition: Deployment ReplicaSet ke through pods manage karta hai. Service label selector se pods ko load-balance karta hai. ConfigMap config, Secret sensitive (base64, encrypted nahi by default).
lessons.why: Daily kaam ke core objects.

lessons.name: K8s Networking — Ingress, CNI, Service Mesh
lessons.desc: Ingress: L7 load balancing with path/host-based routing. CNI: pod networking and network policies. Service mesh: mTLS, traffic management.
lessons.q: How does Kubernetes handle networking? Compare Ingress, CNI, and service mesh.
lessons.qsub: What is mTLS in a service mesh and how does Istio implement it transparently?
lessons.what: Definition: Service types: ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer. Ingress controller (nginx) HTTP routing deta hai. Har pod ka apna IP; CNI pod-to-pod connectivity deta hai.
lessons.why: Traffic flow aur outside exposure samajhne ke liye.
lessons.code:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
spec:
  rules:
  - host: api.example.com
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend: { service: { name: web, port: { number: 80 } } }
gotchas: Ingress resource ke liye controller install hona chahiye
Pod IP ephemeral — Service use karo

lessons.name: Helm, Operators, and CRDs
lessons.desc: Helm: Kubernetes package manager — Charts bundle templates + values. CRD: extends K8s API. Operator: controller that watches CRDs and reconciles state.
lessons.q: What are Helm Charts, CRDs, and Operators? How do they work together?
lessons.qsub: Name popular Kubernetes operators and explain the operator pattern in detail.
lessons.what: Definition: Helm templating se same manifests alag environments mein; Operators (jaise Postgres operator) domain knowledge (backup, failover) automate karte hain.
lessons.why: Bade manifests ko manage aur stateful apps ko run karna.
lessons.code:
$ helm install web ./chart -f values-prod.yaml
$ helm upgrade --install web ./chart --set image.tag=1.2.1
$ helm rollback web 1
$ helm template ./chart | kubectl diff -f -

lessons.name: K8s Security — RBAC, Pod Security, Network Policies
lessons.desc: RBAC: Role-based access control for API operations. Pod Security Standards: privileged, baseline, restricted. NetworkPolicies: pod-level firewall.
lessons.q: How do you secure a Kubernetes cluster? Explain RBAC, Pod Security, and NetworkPolicies.
lessons.qsub: What replaced PodSecurityPolicy and how does Pod Security Admission work at namespace level?
lessons.what: Definition: Least-privilege RBAC, default-deny NetworkPolicy, Pod Security Admission, secrets encryption/external secrets, image policies, audit logs.
lessons.why: Default K8s mein sab pods sab se baat kar sakte hain.
lessons.code:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: { name: default-deny }
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Ingress, Egress]
# phir specific allow rules
gotchas: NetworkPolicy ke liye CNI support chahiye
ServiceAccount token auto-mount band karo jahan zaroorat nahi

lessons.name: Terraform — State, Modules, Workspaces, Providers
lessons.desc: Terraform declares infrastructure in HCL. State file maps config to real resources. Modules encapsulate reusable infrastructure. Workspaces isolate environments.
lessons.q: Explain Terraform state management, modules, and workspaces.
lessons.qsub: How do you store Terraform state remotely and why is state locking important?
terms: Config aur real resources ka mapping.
lessons.what: Definition: Terraform HCL mein desired infra declare karta hai. plan diff dikhata hai, apply change karta hai, state file track karti hai.
lessons.why: Infra versioned, reviewable aur reproducible ban jaata hai.
gotchas: State file mein secrets ho sakte hain
plan review ke bina apply mat karo

lessons.name: Terraform Advanced — Remote State, Locking, Drift Detection
lessons.desc: Remote state stores terraform.tfstate in S3/GCS with DynamoDB locking. Plan detects drift between declared state and real infrastructure.
lessons.q: What is infrastructure drift and how does Terraform detect and handle it?
lessons.qsub: Compare workspace-based vs directory-based state isolation strategies.
lessons.what: Definition: Team ke liye state remote + locked + encrypted. Drift detection scheduled terraform plan se. State split per environment/component.
lessons.why: Local state par teams ek-dusre ka kaam overwrite kar deti hain.
gotchas: Bahut bada state slow — split karo

lessons.name: Configuration Management — Ansible vs Chef vs Puppet
lessons.desc: Ansible: agentless, push-based, YAML playbooks. Chef: agent-based, Ruby DSL, pull-based. Puppet: agent-based, declarative DSL, pull-based.
lessons.q: Compare Ansible, Chef, and Puppet. When would you choose each?
lessons.qsub: How does Packer with cloud-init replace traditional configuration management?
lessons.what: Definition: Config management servers ke andar software/config manage karta hai. Ansible SSH se; Terraform provisioning ke liye, Ansible configuration ke liye.
lessons.why: Servers ko manually configure karna error-prone hai.
lessons.code:
- hosts: web
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: nginx install
      apt: { name: nginx, state: present }
    - name: service on
      service: { name: nginx, state: started, enabled: true }
gotchas: Idempotency ke liye modules use karo, shell kam

lessons.name: Immutable Infrastructure — Packer, AMIs, Golden Images
lessons.desc: Immutable infrastructure: never modify running servers — replace them. Packer builds machine images with everything baked in. Golden images are versioned templates.
lessons.q: What is immutable infrastructure and how does it eliminate configuration drift?
lessons.qsub: How do immutable images compare to container images in terms of deployment and rollback?
lessons.what: Definition: Change = naya image build → naye instances launch → purane terminate. Snowflake servers aur drift khatam.
lessons.why: Reproducible, rollback = pichli image.
gotchas: Image mein secrets bake mat karo

lessons.name: GitOps — ArgoCD, Flux, Declarative Continuous Delivery
lessons.desc: GitOps: Git repo is the single source of truth. ArgoCD/Flux reconciles cluster state with what's in the Git repo. Syncs automatically on commit.
lessons.q: What is GitOps and how does ArgoCD implement it for Kubernetes deployments?
lessons.qsub: How does GitOps enable disaster recovery and what is drift detection in this context?
terms: Cluster khud Git se kheenchta hai.
lessons.what: Definition: Deploy = Git commit/PR. Controller continuously desired state vs live compare karke sync karta hai. Audit trail, rollback = git revert.
lessons.why: CI ko cluster credentials nahi dene padte; drift auto-correct.
gotchas: App repo aur config repo alag rakho
manual kubectl edit revert ho jaayega

lessons.name: Capacity Planning & Auto-scaling — HPA, VPA, Cluster Autoscaler
lessons.desc: HPA: scales pods based on CPU/memory or custom metrics. VPA: adjusts pod resource requests. Cluster autoscaler: adds/removes nodes.
lessons.q: Explain HPA, VPA, and cluster autoscaler. How do they work together?
lessons.qsub: How does Karpenter differ from the standard cluster autoscaler on AWS?
lessons.what: Definition: HPA CPU/custom metrics (RPS, queue depth) par pods scale karta hai. Nodes ke liye Cluster Autoscaler/Karpenter. Load test se baseline set karo.
lessons.why: Traffic spikes mein availability aur off-peak cost saving.
lessons.code:
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
spec:
  scaleTargetRef: { kind: Deployment, name: web }
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 30
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource: { name: cpu, target: { type: Utilization, averageUtilization: 65 } }
gotchas: Requests set na ho to HPA kaam nahi karta
HPA + VPA same metric par conflict
Scale-up delay ke liye min replicas buffer

lessons.name: Disaster Recovery & Backup — RPO, RTO, Multi-region
lessons.desc: RPO: max acceptable data loss. RTO: max acceptable downtime. Multi-region: active-active vs active-passive.
lessons.q: Define RPO and RTO. How do you design a disaster recovery strategy for a cloud application?
lessons.qsub: What is the 3-2-1 backup rule and how does it apply to cloud infrastructure?
terms: Backup/restore, pilot light, warm standby, active-active.
lessons.what: Definition: RPO/RTO business tay karta hai; strategy uske hisaab se (cost badhta jaata hai). Backups ka restore test karna zaroori.
lessons.why: Untested backup = backup nahi.
lessons.code:
RPO 24h/RTO 24h -> backup & restore
RPO 1h/RTO 1h   -> pilot light
RPO ~0/RTO min  -> multi-region active-active
aws rds restore-db-instance-to-point-in-time ...   # drill karo
gotchas: Backups same region/account mein na ho

lessons.name: Chaos Engineering — Principles, GameDays, Tools
lessons.desc: Chaos engineering: proactively inject failures to build confidence in system resilience. Principles: steady state hypothesis, run experiment in production.
lessons.q: What is chaos engineering? How do you run a safe GameDay in production?
lessons.qsub: Compare Chaos Mesh and Litmus for Kubernetes chaos engineering.
lessons.what: Definition: Production-jaisi conditions mein controlled failures (pod kill, latency inject, AZ outage) se weaknesses dhundna. Hypothesis → experiment → learn → fix.
lessons.why: Failure real hone se pehle resilience prove karna.
lessons.code:
# Chaos Mesh / Litmus / Gremlin / AWS FIS
kind: PodChaos
spec: { action: pod-kill, mode: one, selector: { labelSelectors: { app: web } } }
# abort conditions + monitoring ready

lessons.name: Compliance & Audit — SOC2, HIPAA, Policy-as-Code (OPA, Kyverno)
lessons.desc: SOC2: security controls for service providers. HIPAA: healthcare data protection. Policy-as-code: OPA and Kyverno enforce rules as code.
lessons.q: How do you implement policy-as-code in a Kubernetes environment using OPA or Kyverno?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between OPA Gatekeeper and Kyverno for K8s admission control?
terms: Cluster mein enter hone se pehle check.
lessons.what: Definition: Policies code mein: 'koi privileged pod nahi', 'images sirf trusted registry se', 'S3 public nahi'. CI aur admission controller dono par enforce; audit evidence auto.
lessons.why: Manual compliance scale nahi karti.
lessons.code:
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
  - name: no-latest
    match: { any: [{ resources: { kinds: [Pod] } }] }
    validate:
      message: latest tag not allowed
      pattern: { spec: { containers: [{ image: "!*:latest" }] } }
gotchas: Audit mode se shuru, phir enforce

lessons.name: EC2 — instances, AMIs, security groups, key pairs
lessons.desc: EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) provides virtual servers in the cloud. An AMI is a template for an instance (OS + software). Security groups act as virtual firewalls controlling inbound/outbound traffic. Key pairs provide SSH access.
lessons.q: What is an EC2 instance? How do security groups differ from network ACLs?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between an instance store and an EBS volume? When would you use each?
lessons.what: Definition: EC2 virtual servers. Purchasing: On-Demand, Reserved/Savings Plans, Spot. Key pair SSH ke liye (ya SSM Session Manager better). ASG scaling.
lessons.why: AWS compute ka base; interview mein basic.
lessons.code:
aws ec2 run-instances --image-id ami-xxx --instance-type t3.micro \
  --security-group-ids sg-123 --iam-instance-profile Name=app-role
# SSH ke bajaye: aws ssm start-session --target i-abc

lessons.name: S3 — buckets, lifecycle policies, presigned URLs, versioning
lessons.desc: S3 (Simple Storage Service) stores objects (files) in buckets. Lifecycle policies auto-move objects between storage classes (Standard, IA, Glacier). Presigned URLs grant temporary access to private objects. Versioning keeps object history.
lessons.q: What is S3? How do lifecycle policies reduce storage costs?
lessons.qsub: How do presigned URLs work? What is the difference between S3 Standard and S3 IA?
lessons.what: Definition: S3 11 9s durability. Versioning, lifecycle (IA/Glacier), SSE-KMS, Block Public Access, presigned URLs direct upload/download ke liye.
lessons.why: Misconfigured S3 buckets ke breaches famous hain.
cons: Eventual list semantics (ab strong), request costs

lessons.name: RDS — managed databases, Multi-AZ, read replicas, backups
lessons.desc: RDS (Relational Database Service) manages PostgreSQL, MySQL, etc. Multi-AZ provides automatic failover for high availability. Read replicas scale read traffic. Automated backups enable point-in-time recovery.
lessons.q: What is RDS? How does Multi-AZ differ from Read Replicas?
lessons.qsub: When would you use Aurora Serverless vs a provisioned RDS instance?
lessons.what: Definition: RDS managed backups, patching, failover. Multi-AZ availability ke liye, read replicas performance ke liye — dono alag cheezein.
lessons.why: Database ops offload, par design decisions phir bhi aapke.
lessons.code:
aws rds create-db-instance --engine postgres --multi-az --storage-encrypted \
  --backup-retention-period 7 --db-instance-class db.t3.medium ...
# app connection pooling (RDS Proxy) lambda ke liye

lessons.name: Lambda — serverless functions, cold starts, event sources
lessons.desc: Lambda runs code without managing servers. Triggered by events (API Gateway, S3, SQS, DynamoDB streams). Cold start = first invocation delay. Provisioned concurrency eliminates cold starts at extra cost.
lessons.q: What is AWS Lambda? What causes cold starts and how do you mitigate them?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between synchronous and asynchronous Lambda invocations? How does Lambda handle retries?
terms: Naye execution environment ka startup delay.
lessons.what: Definition: Lambda event aane par code chalata hai, per-invocation billing. Limits: 15 min, memory 10GB. Provisioned concurrency cold start kam karta hai.
lessons.why: Spiky/event-driven workloads mein ops aur cost bachta hai.
gotchas: SQS retries se duplicate — idempotent banao

lessons.name: VPC — subnets, route tables, NAT gateway, internet gateway
lessons.desc: VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) is your isolated network in AWS. Public subnets have internet access via Internet Gateway. Private subnets use NAT Gateway for outbound-only internet. Route tables control traffic flow between subnets.
lessons.q: What is a VPC? How do public and private subnets differ?
lessons.qsub: When do you need a NAT Gateway vs an Internet Gateway? How do VPC peering and Transit Gateway differ?
lessons.what: Definition: VPC mein CIDR, subnets (multi-AZ), route tables, IGW (internet), NAT GW (private se bahar), VPC endpoints (AWS services bina internet).
lessons.why: Secure network foundation.
gotchas: CIDR overlap peering block karta hai

lessons.name: IAM — users, roles, policies, least privilege
lessons.desc: IAM (Identity and Access Management) controls who can do what. Users have long-term credentials. Roles provide temporary credentials (for EC2, Lambda, etc.). Policies are JSON documents granting/denying permissions. Least privilege = only grant what is needed.
lessons.q: What is IAM? What is the difference between an IAM user and an IAM role?
lessons.qsub: How do you implement least privilege in practice? What is an IAM policy evaluation logic?
lessons.what: Definition: Users ke liye SSO/MFA, workloads ke liye roles (instance profile, IRSA), long-lived access keys avoid. Explicit Deny > Allow. Access Analyzer unused permissions batata hai.
lessons.why: Cloud security ka #1 control.
gotchas: Root user MFA aur use nahi

lessons.name: CloudWatch — metrics, logs, alarms, dashboards
lessons.desc: CloudWatch collects metrics (CPU, memory, request count), logs (Lambda, EC2, RDS), and alarms (notify when threshold breached). Dashboards visualize metrics. CloudWatch Events/EventBridge route events between services.
lessons.q: How do you set up an alarm for high CPU on an EC2 instance using CloudWatch?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between CloudWatch Logs Insights and CloudWatch Metrics?
lessons.what: Definition: CloudWatch metrics, logs, alarms, dashboards. Custom metrics, composite alarms. Memory/disk ke liye agent chahiye.
lessons.why: Observability ke bina incident detect nahi hota.
lessons.code:
aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm --alarm-name 5xx-high --metric-name HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count \
  --namespace AWS/ApplicationELB --statistic Sum --period 60 --evaluation-periods 5 \
  --threshold 50 --comparison-operator GreaterThanThreshold --alarm-actions $SNS_ARN
# Logs Insights: fields @timestamp, @message | filter @message like /ERROR/ | limit 20

lessons.name: ALB & ELB — load balancing, health checks, target groups
lessons.desc: ALB (Application Load Balancer) routes HTTP/HTTPS traffic to targets (EC2, Lambda, IP). ELB is the umbrella name. Health checks ensure traffic only goes to healthy targets. Target groups define which instances receive traffic.
lessons.q: What is the difference between ALB and NLB? When would you use each?
lessons.qsub: How do sticky sessions work with ALB? What is the difference between path-based and host-based routing?
lessons.what: Definition: ALB path/host routing, WebSocket, WAF integration. Health checks unhealthy targets nikalte hain. Connection draining deployments mein.
lessons.why: HA aur zero-downtime deploys.
lessons.code:
TargetGroup: health check GET /health -> 200, interval 10s, healthy 2, unhealthy 3
Listener 443: /api/* -> tg-api ; default -> tg-web
deregistration_delay = 30s
gotchas: Health check endpoint DB-heavy na ho
Sticky sessions scaling hurt karti hain

lessons.name: Serverless — Lambda, API Gateway, event-driven architecture
lessons.desc: Serverless = no server management. AWS Lambda, Azure Functions, GCP Cloud Run. API Gateway routes HTTP to Lambda. Event-driven: S3, SQS, DynamoDB streams trigger functions. Cold starts, execution limits (15min Lambda), vendor lock-in.
lessons.q: What are the limitations of serverless? When should you NOT use serverless?
lessons.qsub: What is cold start and how do you minimize it? How does API Gateway + Lambda compare to a traditional REST server?
lessons.what: Definition: Serverless mein infra management provider ka; auto-scale, per-ms billing. Patterns: API GW+Lambda, S3→Lambda, queue workers, step functions.
lessons.why: Chhoti teams ke liye fast delivery.
lessons.code:
API Gateway -> Lambda -> DynamoDB
S3 upload -> Lambda -> thumbnail
SQS -> Lambda (batch, DLQ)
Step Functions: orchestration
gotchas: Steady high traffic par containers sasti ho sakti hain

lessons.name: Cloud Networking — VPC, subnets, security groups, load balancers
lessons.desc: VPC isolates your cloud network. Public subnets have internet access. Private subnets are internal only. Security groups are stateful firewalls. NACLs are stateless. ALB for HTTP routing. NLB for TCP/UDP. NAT Gateway for private subnet internet access.
lessons.q: What is the difference between a security group and a NACL?
lessons.qsub: How do you design a VPC for a multi-tier application? What is the difference between ALB and NLB?
lessons.what: Definition: Public/private subnets, SG vs NACL, LB layers (L4/L7), DNS (Route53), CDN, VPN/peering/Transit Gateway.
lessons.why: Architecture interviews mein standard topic.
lessons.code:
Internet -> CloudFront -> ALB (public) -> ECS (private) -> RDS (private)
SG chain: alb-sg -> app-sg -> db-sg
gotchas: SG referencing SG use karo, IP nahi
DNS TTL failover ko slow karta hai

lessons.name: Cloud Cost Optimization — Reserved Instances, Spot, right-sizing
lessons.desc: Reserved Instances: 1-3 year commitments for 30-60% discount. Spot Instances: up to 90% discount but can be terminated. Right-sizing: match instance type to workload. Savings Plans: flexible commitment. Cost allocation tags for per-team billing.
lessons.q: How do you reduce AWS costs by 50%? What is the difference between Reserved Instances and Savings Plans?
lessons.qsub: When should you use Spot Instances vs Reserved Instances? How do you implement cost allocation tags?
terms: Instance size usage ke hisaab se.
lessons.what: Definition: Pehle visibility (tags, Cost Explorer), phir right-size, idle resources delete, commitment discounts steady load par, spot fault-tolerant workloads par, storage tiering, data transfer kam.
lessons.why: Cloud bill chupke se badhta hai.
lessons.code:
Tag: team, env, service  -> cost allocation
Compute Optimizer / Trust Advisor se rightsizing
Spot for batch/CI; On-demand + savings plan for baseline
S3 lifecycle -> IA/Glacier; delete unattached EBS/IPs
gotchas: NAT aur data transfer hidden costs

lessons.name: Feature Flags — progressive delivery, A/B testing, kill switches
lessons.desc: Feature flags control feature visibility without deployment. Progressive delivery: gradual rollout (1% → 10% → 100%). A/B testing: split traffic between variants. Kill switches: instantly disable broken features. Tools: LaunchDarkly, Unleash, Flagsmith.
lessons.q: How do feature flags enable progressive delivery? What is the difference between release flags and experiment flags?
lessons.qsub: How do you implement feature flags without adding technical debt? What is the risk of too many flags?
lessons.what: Definition: Flags runtime par behaviour badalte hain bina deploy. Use: gradual rollout, A/B, kill switch, ops toggles. Flag ka lifecycle: create → rollout → cleanup.
lessons.why: Deploy aur release decouple; risk kam.
gotchas: Flag service down hone par fallback
